value.produces: assets/vision (the sandbox rootfs with PCE built from the pinned hampa.ch tarball under /opt/pce, pce.cfg, the XT ROMs) and assets/vision/disk (hd0.pbi with Visi On installed + VOAPP1/2.psi, the copy-protected key disks; cold-boot reset)

labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE, SANDBOXED: PCE (hampa.ch, GPL) pce-ibmpc runs inside a systemd-nspawn container with private PID/mount/net/IPC/UTS/user namespaces (host uid base 2162688, --volatile=overlay over a debootstrap minbase trixie rootfs, --private-network, capabilities dropped, @mount filtered, --no-new-privileges; the operator's host-application rule after the medley incident) an IBM 5160 XT (8088 @ 4.77 MHz, 640 KB, CGA, two 360 KB floppies, 10 MB XT fixed disk, Mouse Systems serial mouse on COM1) booting PC-DOS 2.00 into VisiCorp Visi On 1.0, inside a pinned 1280x800 Xvfb on :94; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11). PCE's x11 terminal draws CGA at scale 2 with its 4/3 aspect correction, so 640x200 becomes exactly 1280x800 and the Xvfb root IS the PCE window — root coordinates are window coordinates, no crop, no offset. No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel, no network (Visi On on PC-DOS 2.00 has no TCP/IP stack; the container has lo only). Keys: XTEST. COPY PROTECTION: VOAPP1.psi is the key disk and must be in A: whenever Visi On starts; it ships as PCE's own .psi (converted from the TransCopy .TC dump with PCE's psi tool) because the protection lives in the flux. Reset=relaunch: fresh copies of hd0.pbi + VOAPP1/2.psi from assets/vision/disk and a cold boot of the XT; vision-inner.sh types VISION at the C:\> prompt. PCE's monitor is on FIFOs under the station's work/ (mon.in / mon.out) for disk swaps (`di 0 /work/VOAPP2.psi`). Drive it with xdotool on DISPLAY=:94 from labrun, or `labctl shot vision`. See docs/lab/VISION-WAVE.md.

museum.periodBrowser: none — December 1983, a decade before the web, and Visi On has no network stack at all
museum.blurb: VisiCorp shipped Visi On in December 1983 and beat both the Macintosh and Windows to the IBM PC: overlapping windows, a mouse, pull-down menus and a Services window that installs and launches applications, all running on an 8088 with a CGA card and 640 KB. It cost $1,795 plus a hard disk and a mouse nobody had yet, it ran only VisiCorp's own three programs, and it sold almost nothing — but the command strip along the bottom of this screen (HELP, CLOSE, OPEN, FULL, FRAME, OPTIONS, TRANSFER, STOP) is the graphical desktop arriving on the PC a full year early.
museum.notes: Live streamhost station, HOST-NATIVE and SANDBOXED from birth: PCE (Hampa Hug, GPLv2+) emulates an IBM 5160 XT inside a systemd-nspawn container with private PID/mount/net/IPC/UTS/user namespaces (host uid base 2162688, --volatile=overlay over a debootstrap minbase trixie rootfs, --private-network, capabilities dropped, @mount filtered, --no-new-privileges; the operator's host-application rule after the medley incident), on a pinned 1280x800 Xvfb; the daemon captures the X root and drives XTEST. The Xvfb root IS PCE's window (CGA 640x200 at scale 2 with 4/3 aspect correction = 1280x800 exactly). Visi On's copy protection makes VOAPP1 a key disk that must sit in A: at every start, which is why the station ships PCE .psi images converted from the TransCopy .TC dumps rather than plain sector images. Reset = relaunch: fresh disk copies and a cold boot of the XT, then VISION typed at the C:\> prompt. No network of any kind. spa.pointerRel is false: the emulated mouse is Mouse Systems-relative hardware, but the no-grab patch's mouse_div_x=2/mouse_div_y=4 makes the browser's x11test-abs injection land 1:1 on the guest cursor, and the router requires pointerRel=false for that backend (validator: type=4 relative injection bypasses the router entirely). See docs/lab/VISION-WAVE.md and docs/guests/vision.md.

emulator.version: 20250420-cc0c583c (hampa.ch git snapshot), built from source inside the station's own sandbox rootfs
emulator.driver: pce-ibmpc, system model 5160 (IBM PC XT), boot=128, CGA, 8250 on COM1 with a Mouse Systems mouse

network.note: No network device of any kind. Visi On runs on PC-DOS 2.00 (1983) and has no TCP/IP stack, PCE's 5160 has no emulated NIC configured, and the container runs with --private-network so the only interface inside is lo. No retronet reservation was taken — it would be meaningless here.

reset.fixture: Visi On 1.0 at rest: the stippled Visi On desktop with the Services window open on Archives, its `start install remove Printing` menu line, and the command strip along the bottom (HELP CLOSE OPEN FULL FRAME OPTIONS TRANSFER STOP). resetMode=relaunch with no save state — PCE's ibmpc has none: the launcher copies hd0.pbi (Visi On installed) and VOAPP1/2.psi fresh from assets/vision/disk, cold-boots the 5160, and vision-inner.sh types VISION at the C:\> prompt once the screen settles.
